rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods and Results <U+2013> the authors report their own stakeholder interview survey (>170 stakeholders in six EU countries) on the adoption of remote sensing in agriculture, including estimates of remotely sensed area per country and a SWOT analysis of adoption factors.
rows.notes: The study is an adoption survey of remote sensing (satellites, UAVs, aircraft) value chains; it does not study soil sensors or precision irrigation systems, does not measure water use or water conservation outcomes, and does not concern organic systems. The only irrigation mention is that stakeholders in Spain reported remote sensing being used to generate irrigation maps for corn and some wineries, which is an adoption observation, not a result on water-use optimisation. Technology and effect both differ from the claim.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods and Results <U+2013> own interview-based survey of >170 remote sensing value-chain stakeholders in France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Slovakia and Spain, with country-level estimates of remotely sensed area and adoption barriers.
rows.notes: The study reports nothing on soil sensors, precision irrigation, soil fertility or soil health, nor on organic systems. It documents remote sensing adoption patterns (platforms, crops, uses such as N prescription maps from vegetation indices, area covered, SWOT factors). No own result on the claimed technology or effect.

notes: Conference paper (ECPA 2023) reporting a stakeholder interview survey on remote sensing adoption across six EU countries; figures 1 and 2 are not included in the text but their absence does not affect the ratings. The study is cited for a claim about soil sensors and precision irrigation that it does not address.
